title: Laughlin quasihole geometry from a single snapshot ensemble
abstract: Can a probability distribution measured in one basis determine complex quantum geometry? The answer is affirmative for a lattice Laughlin quasihole. The exact occupation law at one generic reference position, together with the known analytic quasihole factor, fixes the complete complex Gram kernel. A finite snapshot ensemble estimates this kernel without preparing another member of the family, and thereby determines finite-distance overlaps, Bargmann phases, the quantum metric, and the Berry curvature. The same analytic structure confines the family to an exact projective subspace whose dimension grows at most linearly with particle number. Exact enumeration of a Nielsen-Cirac-Sierra state demonstrates finite-shot reconstruction of both the metric and a geometric phase. Moreover, a Rényi-2 divergence sets the statistical range of the reconstruction while, at nondegenerate points, occupation readout also attains the local single-copy multiparameter information bound.
summary: This work demonstrates that the complex quantum geometry of lattice Laughlin quasihole states can be fully determined from measuring the occupation probability distribution at just one reference point. By exploiting the known analytic structure of the state amplitudes, the authors reconstruct the quantum metric and Berry curvature, showing that single-shot measurements are surprisingly powerful tools for characterizing quantum geometry.
main_problem: The central problem is determining complex quantum geometric properties, such as the quantum metric and Berry curvature, using only a single probability distribution measurement (snapshot) from a lattice Laughlin quasihole state.
main_result: A single snapshot measurement is sufficient to reconstruct the complete complex Gram kernel, thereby fixing the quantum metric and Berry curvature of the state family.
method: The reconstruction relies on a single-reference kernel identity, using the known analytic quasihole factor and the measured occupation probability $P_0(n)$ to determine the overlap kernel $K(w, v)$.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by lattice Laughlin quasihole states, parameterized by the quasihole position $w$, whose amplitudes factorize based on the occupation configuration $n$.
key_observables: Quantum metric coefficient $G(w)$, Berry curvature $\Omega_{xy}$, Overlap Kernel $K(w, v)$, and the Connes distance $d_\Lambda$.
important_parameters: The reconstruction is limited by the Rényi-2 divergence $D_2(P_w\|P_0)$ and the local single-copy multiparameter information bound.
main_assumptions: The reconstruction critically depends on the known analytic structure of the quasihole factor $f_n(w)$ and assumes the reference point $w_0$ is generic.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the reconstruction of the scalar metric coefficient $G(w)$ both analytically and numerically, alongside the singular values of the state matrix.
paper_structure: The paper develops a kernel identity from the single snapshot measurement, uses this identity to derive geometric quantities like the metric and distance, and finally analyzes the statistical limitations using divergence measures.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, non-standard method to extract full geometric information (metric, curvature) from minimal quantum measurements, which is highly relevant for characterizing complex many-body ground states.
